answer: Jurors commit before they see votes: each grader posts a hash of its score while the epoch is open, then reveals only after every commitment seals. A clone farm gains nothing from a synchronised sonnet of identities, because no member can read the emerging consensus before committing. Every reveal is signed and slashable, so faking a crowd means paying stake per head for blind guesses and losing it when those guesses diverge. Honest judgment seeps through a karst of contested grades and drains the meadow of fake seats.
